newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom, Mercantile profits up, May weaker.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom, Mercantile profits up, May weaker.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc. and Mercantile Stores Co. Inc. Monday reported higher quarterly earnings, but May Department Stores Co.'s performance deteriorated slightly.

Nordstrom's net earnings rose 15.6 percent to $34.0 million, or 42 cents a share in its fiscal third quarter ended Oct. 31, from $29.4 million, or 36 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales grew 8.6 percent to $984.4 million from $906.8 million.
"Our third-quarter performance reflects an improvement in merchandise margins and expense management," said John Goesling, executive vice president.
During the quarter, Seattle-based Nordstrom completed its expansion programme for the year with new store openings in Detroit and Denver. Nordstrom has 83 stores in 17 states.

Mercantile's profits rose 6.4 percent to $31.1 million, or 85 cents per share, in the third quarter ended Nov. 2, from $29.2 million, or 79 cents per share, in the year-ago period. Revenues grew to $727.7 million from $694.8 million.

Pre-opening costs for four new stores that opened in October reduced the latest results by 2 cents a share. However, Fairfield, Ohio-based Mercantile said it expects the new stores to boost fourth-quarter earnings.
May Department Stores said its profits fell to $118 million, or 44 cents a share, in the quarter ended Nov. 2 from $135 million, or 50 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Revenues rose to $2.9 billion from $2.6 billion, while net retail sales grew to $2.8 billion from $2.5 billion.
Nordstrom's stock was unchanged at $40.375 on Nasdaq. Mercantile rose 25 cents to $51.875 and May slid $1.125 to $48.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
